subject: astronomy
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: On the celestial sphere, right ascension is the equivalent of which Earth coordinate?
questions.explain: Right ascension measures position around the celestial equator, just as longitude does on Earth.

questions.q: The apparent yearly path of the Sun across the celestial sphere is called the:
questions.explain: The ecliptic is the Sun's apparent annual path, tilted about 23.5 degrees to the celestial equator.

questions.q: Reflecting telescopes are generally preferred over refracting telescopes for very large instruments because mirrors:
options: Can be supported from behind and do not suffer chromatic aberration
questions.explain: Large mirrors can be supported across their backs and, unlike lenses, do not split colours (chromatic aberration), so reflectors scale to huge sizes.

questions.q: A leap year, with 366 days, is added because:
options: Of changes in the Earth's tilt
The Moon adds an extra day
The Earth's orbit is slowing down
The year is about 365.25 days, so an extra day keeps the calendar aligned
questions.explain: Earth orbits the Sun in roughly 365.25 days, so an extra day every four years keeps the calendar in step.

questions.q: The magnification of a telescope is found by:
options: Dividing the focal length of the objective by that of the eyepiece
Adding the focal lengths of the objective and eyepiece
Dividing the aperture by the focal length
questions.explain: Magnification equals objective focal length divided by eyepiece focal length.

questions.q: Coordinated Universal Time (UT/GMT) is based on the local time at:
questions.explain: Universal Time is the mean solar time at the Greenwich meridian, the basis for world time zones.

questions.q: In the horizontal coordinate system, azimuth measures the:
options: Compass bearing around the horizon (usually from north)
questions.explain: Azimuth is measured around the horizon, conventionally clockwise from due north.

questions.q: Which type of telescope is usually placed in space to observe radiation that is absorbed by the Earth's atmosphere, such as X-rays?
options: An X-ray telescope on a satellite
questions.explain: X-rays are blocked by the atmosphere, so X-ray telescopes must be flown above it on satellites in space.

questions.q: Increasing the aperture (diameter) of a telescope's objective mainly improves its ability to:
options: Collect more light and resolve finer detail
Increase the field of view only
questions.explain: A larger aperture gathers more light and improves resolving power, showing fainter, sharper detail.

questions.q: A telescope has an objective of focal length 1000 mm and an eyepiece of focal length 20 mm. Its magnification is:
questions.explain: Magnification = focal length of objective / focal length of eyepiece = 1000 / 20 = 50.

questions.q: Stars appear to move across the night sky from east to west mainly because:
options: The Earth rotates on its axis from west to east
questions.explain: The apparent nightly motion of the stars is caused by the Earth's west-to-east rotation.

questions.q: On the celestial sphere, declination is the equivalent of which Earth coordinate?
questions.explain: Declination measures angular distance north or south of the celestial equator, like latitude on Earth.

questions.q: A reflecting telescope gathers light using a:
questions.explain: A reflector uses a concave primary mirror, avoiding the lens problems of large refractors.

questions.q: Astronomical 'seeing' refers to:
options: The blurring and twinkling of images caused by atmospheric turbulence
questions.explain: Seeing describes image steadiness; turbulent air makes stars twinkle and blurs fine detail.

questions.q: Why do observatories often place very large telescopes on high mountains?
options: To get above much of the atmosphere, reducing absorption and improving seeing
To be closer to the stars
questions.explain: High, dry mountain sites have thinner, more stable air and less light pollution, improving observations.

questions.q: Radio telescopes typically have very large dishes because radio waves:
options: Have long wavelengths, so a big aperture is needed for good resolution
questions.explain: Resolving power depends on aperture compared with wavelength, so the long wavelengths of radio waves require very large dishes.

questions.q: On the celestial sphere, the celestial equator is:
options: The line joining the celestial poles
The path the Sun appears to follow over a year
A projection of the Earth's equator onto the sky
questions.explain: The celestial equator is the Earth's equator projected outward onto the celestial sphere.

questions.q: The constellations of the zodiac are special because:
options: They are the brightest in the sky
The Sun, Moon and planets appear to move through them along the ecliptic
questions.explain: The zodiac constellations lie along the ecliptic, the band through which the Sun, Moon and planets move.

questions.q: Light pollution is a problem for astronomers because it:
options: Brightens the night sky and hides faint objects
questions.explain: Artificial light scatters in the atmosphere, washing out faint stars and reducing contrast.

questions.q: In the altitude-azimuth (horizontal) coordinate system, altitude measures:
options: The angle of an object above the horizon
The compass direction along the horizon
questions.explain: Altitude is the angle above the horizon, from 0 degrees at the horizon to 90 degrees at the zenith.

questions.q: Which group of stars are used by Northern Hemisphere observers to locate Polaris, the Pole Star?
options: The pointer stars of the Plough (Ursa Major)
questions.explain: The two 'pointer' stars at the end of the Plough (part of Ursa Major) line up with Polaris.

questions.q: A refracting telescope forms its image using a:
questions.explain: A refractor uses a convex objective lens to gather and focus light; a reflector uses a mirror.
